court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: First Additional Family Court, Chennai (M.C.No.90 of 2012)
case_name: Tekepat Satish Chandra Menon vs Asha Panickar

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Tekepat Satish Chandra Menon, former husband and father
parties.respondent_defendant: Asha Panickar, mother and natural guardian of Uday Krishnan Menon

facts_of_case: The petitioner is the former husband and father who filed a criminal revision case to set aside an order denying his relief claims.

legal_principles.principle: A wife who has agreed not to claim maintenance in future is not entitled to maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
legal_principles.held: According to the learned Counsel for the petitioner, he would submit that this is a case where the wife is living separately on account of the dissolution of marriage by mutual consent between the parties. Once the wife is living separately on mutual consent and it has been specifically agreed by her in the mutual consent petition that she will not claim any maintenance in future, she is not entitled to maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

legal_principles.principle: A father has a duty to maintain his child, especially if the child is special.
legal_principles.held: The learned Counsel would further submit that as far as the maintenance of the child is concerned, since the child is a special child, it is the duty of the father to maintain.

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the appeal and set aside the trial court's order.
